task: Find all assays of small molecules concerning immune-context amplification and perturbational molecular signatures related to liver stress. This includes molecule-induced cytokine sensitization, inflammasome activation, hepatocyte–immune-cell interactions, DAMP signaling, and transcriptomic, metabolomic, lipidomic, miRNA, or extracellular-vesicle responses after molecule exposure. Make sure to include assays such as drug-plus-TNF, IFN-γ, or LPS challenge, hepatocyte–THP-1 or PBMC coculture, conditioned-medium inflammasome assays, lymphocyte activation assays, RNA sequencing, expression panels, metabolomics, lipidomics, and extracellular-vesicle profiling. Specify molecule and immune-stimulus dose and units, treatment sequence and duration, Cmax multiple, assay and coculture format, cell ratio, species, human donor and HLA information when available, liver-cell model and metabolic competence, sampling time, analytical platform, normalization method, and outputs such as cytokine concentration, caspase-1 activity, viability synergy, fold change, pathway score, metabolite abundance, AUC, sensitivity, or specificity. Include all key experimental details.
task_instantiation:
Extract every primary experiment performed in the paper in which the focal entity identified by the supplied top-level global_identifier is a named, chemically defined small molecule, drug, xenobiotic, endogenous metabolite or lipid, or defined small-molecule mixture/formulation, and the exposure produces either (a) an immune-context effect relevant to liver stress or (b) a perturbational molecular signature explicitly relevant to hepatic stress, injury, or DILI. Do not copy the global_identifier into a field. Preserve a paper code, salt/formulation, or mixture name in extra_details only when needed to interpret the exposure.

In scope are molecule-plus-TNF, IFN-gamma, LPS, Con A, GalN/LPS, CpG, poly I:C, Fas/death-receptor, PAMP, DAMP, inflammasome-priming/trigger, lymphocyte, or analogous challenge assays; cytokine sensitization, amplification, suppression, or null interaction; inflammasome, caspase-1, pyroptosis, DAMP or innate-receptor signaling; hepatocyte interactions with Kupffer cells, macrophages, THP-1 cells, PBMCs, monocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes/NKT/T cells, stellate cells, or LSECs; direct coculture, transwell, conditioned-medium, apoptotic-body or EV transfer; spheroids, organoids, liver chips or other microphysiological systems; precision-cut slices, perfused liver, ex vivo cells, whole-animal liver models, and administered human exposures with post-exposure liver-relevant profiling. Also include molecule-induced targeted expression, RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, microarray, metabolomic, lipidomic, miRNA, proteomic/signaling, secretome, immune-phenotype, and extracellular-vesicle responses when the paper explicitly links the measured signature to liver stress. Include increased, decreased, protective, sensitizing, null, inactive, mixed, non-monotonic, and below-detection findings.

Exclude experiments with no qualifying small-molecule exposure; challenge-only experiments in which the sole perturbation is a cytokine, protein, peptide, antibody, oligonucleotide, genetic manipulation, LPS, Con A, cell, EV, pathogen, surgery, diet, nanoparticle without defined small-molecule cargo, crude botanical extract, or undefined mixture. Such agents may be secondary stimuli or model context. Exclude routine assay probes, stains, solvents, vehicles, substrates, and analytical standards unless their biological effect is itself evaluated. Exclude generic non-liver immune assays; unrelated organ or tumor assays; pharmacokinetics, uptake, metabolism, receptor binding, purified-enzyme activity, generic viability/apoptosis, oxidative stress, ALT/AST, histology, fibrosis, survival, or injury-only studies unless the same condition includes a qualifying immune interaction or molecular signature. Exclude observational biomarker studies without administered or ex vivo small-molecule exposure, methods or protocols with no linked result, purely computational predictions, proposed mechanisms without direct testing, reviews, background claims, cited prior work, unpublished/not-shown results, and assay descriptions that cannot be linked to an exposure and measured outcome in this paper.

Create one record per focal molecule x exact molecule exposure/regimen x secondary immune or liver-stress stimulus condition x biological model and physical format x sampling time x endpoint/analyte or coherent signature x reported output metric/comparator. Split when a distinct reported result differs in molecule, dose, stimulus or stimulus dose, sequence, species/model, donor-specific condition, coculture format, sampling time, endpoint/analyte, platform-derived metric, comparator, or effect direction. Merge technical replicates and repeated descriptions of the same experiment. Do not create records for vehicle, untreated, challenge-only, or positive-control arms unless the focal small molecule itself is the independently evaluated entity; represent their use as the comparator on the treated record.

For dose-response studies, split doses only when dose-specific results are reported. If only a range, series, trend, EC50, fitted AUC, or collective conclusion is reported, create one record, leave molecule_dose_value and molecule_dose_unit null, and preserve the exact series and qualifier in extra_details. For targeted multiplex panels, split analytes when each has a distinct value, direction, time, metric, or platform; otherwise retain one panel record with a shared conclusion. For untargeted or high-dimensional transcriptomic, metabolomic, lipidomic, miRNA, proteomic, or EV data, do not create inferred rows for every feature: create records for explicitly highlighted features with reported results and for each explicitly reported pathway, panel, classifier, performance result, or coherent global signature. Split a fixed mixture into constituents only when they were tested separately; otherwise treat the defined mixture as the focal entity.

Require explicit textual, table, figure-legend, or unambiguously linked methods-and-results evidence that the exposure occurred and the endpoint was measured in this paper. Extract only explicit statements and direct arithmetic requiring no biological assumption. Do not infer molecule or stimulus identity, dose, unit, route, simultaneity or sequence, duration, sampling time, species, cell ratio, donor attributes, HLA/MHC, metabolic competence, platform, normalization, significance, mechanism, Cmax multiple, or numeric result from general knowledge. Standard abbreviation expansion and species identification from an explicitly named standard cell line are allowed; metabolic competence is never inferred from a cell-line reputation. Preserve reported dose, time, and result units without conversion. Do not calculate Cmax multiples, fold changes, synergy, AUC, sensitivity, or specificity unless the paper explicitly reports them. Do not digitize figures.

Use molecule_dose_value only for one exact result-linked number and molecule_dose_unit only for its reported unit. In immune_stimulus_regimen, record every secondary challenge component with its dose, unit, and route when stated. In exposure_schedule, record the molecule route, exact chronological order, pretreatment/cotreatment/post-treatment, transfer direction, intervals, exposure and challenge durations, washout, repeated-dose frequency, sampling time relative to the relevant exposure, and an explicitly reported Cmax multiple. In experimental_system, record setting, species by component, liver and immune models, primary versus cell-line status, direct/transwell/transfer architecture, producer and recipient roles, labeled cell ratio, donor count/status/pooling, HLA or MHC facts, and explicit hepatic metabolic competence. In analytical_platform_and_normalization, record the measurement platform and normalization/reference procedure exactly as reported.

In assay_family, classify the biological endpoint class only, never the platform or the design; a classifier or assay-performance result takes the family of its underlying measurement, with AUC, sensitivity, or specificity recorded in endpoint_and_comparator, result_value, and result_unit. Use other_qualifying_endpoint only for a stated endpoint class that no listed value fits, and name that class in extra_details. Record an explicitly tested interaction claim such as sensitization, synergy, suppression, or protection in endpoint_and_comparator, and use effect_direction only for the direction of the endpoint itself; use mixed for opposing directions across panel members, doses, or times, including biphasic responses, and preserve the exact pattern in extra_details. For a qualitative result, populate effect_direction and leave result_value and result_unit null. For a quantitative result, record the treatment effect or performance value—not an unrelated baseline—and its separate unit or metric label. Preserve inequalities, ranges, mean plus/minus error, confidence intervals, thresholds, detection limits, group values, and whether a value was directly reported or trivially calculated in extra_details. Use below_detection only when that is the reported outcome and preserve the detection limit if supplied.

Assume only ordinary matched vehicle/untreated controls, standard normoxic serum-containing culture, and routine animal husbandry as documentation defaults; do not treat defaults as evidence or write them into fields. Never assume timing, route, donor/HLA status, metabolic competence, or normalization. Put material generalizability limits and nondefault conditions in extra_details, including disease/injury or genetic background, diet or fasting, sex/age restriction, unusual medium/oxygen/flow, serum starvation, cross-species systems, sensitization or priming, supra-physiologic exposure, donor selection, unusual formulation, nanoparticles/liposomes, unresolved dose series, and calculated values. Also use extra_details for strain, genotype, vehicle/formulation, medium, plating density, sample size, replicate/error/statistical information, p values, assay vendor, instrument settings, sample preparation, EV isolation, chromatography, gating, detection limits, ancillary ALT/AST or histology, secondary pathways/features, and mechanistic observations that do not merit their own record. Never write not reported, unspecified, unclear, not applicable, or similar missingness text; leave the relevant field null.

schema_spec.name: molecule_dose_value
schema_spec.description: Single numeric dose or concentration of the focal small molecule for this record, exactly as reported and without conversion. Split dose-specific results. For an unresolved range or series with only an aggregate result, leave this field null and preserve the series in extra_details. Missing or unstated dose is null, never a placeholder value.

schema_spec.name: molecule_dose_unit
schema_spec.description: Reported unit corresponding to molecule_dose_value, preserved without conversion. This field is meaningful only as the pair of molecule_dose_value: leave it null whenever molecule_dose_value is null, and also when a dose value is reported with no stated unit. The vocabulary is open because the candidate schemas supplied inconsistent and incomplete unit sets; do not use other, dose_not_quantified, not_reported, or similar placeholders.

schema_spec.name: immune_stimulus_regimen
schema_spec.description: Complete secondary immune challenge, sensitizer, DAMP/PAMP, transferred conditioned medium or vesicle preparation, or nonimmune liver-stress regimen paired with the focal molecule, including each component's name, dose or concentration, unit, and route when stated; for example 'TNF-alpha 10 ng/mL' or 'D-GalN 700 mg/kg i.p. + LPS 10 ug/kg i.v.'. For transfer designs, record here what was transferred and how it was dosed or diluted; the producer-to-recipient architecture belongs in experimental_system. Null for a molecule-only signature assay or when no secondary stimulus is stated. Do not write none or not reported.

schema_spec.name: exposure_schedule
schema_spec.description: Concise chronology of the focal-molecule route and dosing, stimulus order, pretreatment or cotreatment, transfer steps, intervals, exposure/challenge duration, washout, repeat frequency, and sampling time relative to exposure. Include an explicitly reported Cmax multiple here; never calculate one. Null when no schedule information is supplied, without a missingness placeholder.

schema_spec.name: experimental_system
schema_spec.description: Complete test system and physical assay format: in vitro/ex vivo/in vivo/human setting; species for each component; liver and immune cell/tissue models; primary versus line status; monoculture, direct or transwell coculture, conditioned-medium/EV transfer, slice, organoid/chip, perfused organ, animal, or clinical format; producer-to-recipient direction; labeled cell ratio; disease/genetic context; human donor count/status/pooling; explicit HLA/MHC; and explicit hepatic metabolic competence. Describe the architecture here and the identity and dose of any transferred or administered stimulus in immune_stimulus_regimen. Do not infer unreported properties. Null only if the paper supplies none of these details; never encode not stated as text.

schema_spec.name: assay_family
schema_spec.description: Principal biological class of the measured endpoint, not the experimental design and not the measurement technology. Choose exactly one, using this precedence when more than one could apply: (1) if the reported dataset is a named high-dimensional survey, use transcriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, mirna, or extracellular_vesicle; (2) otherwise use the specific innate-immune class - inflammasome_or_pyroptosis for caspase-1, NLRP3, gasdermin, or pyroptotic endpoints, damp_or_innate_signaling only when DAMP release or innate-receptor (for example TLR) engagement is itself the reported endpoint; (3) otherwise use cytokine_chemokine_or_eicosanoid for secreted mediator levels, immune_cell_function for activation, polarization, recruitment, phenotyping, lymphocyte responses, or immune-cell-mediated cytotoxicity, and cell_viability_death_or_synergy for hepatocyte injury, death, or drug-challenge synergy; (4) otherwise use targeted_gene_expression for gene- or panel-level transcript measurement and protein_signaling_or_enzyme_activity for signaling-protein abundance or phosphorylation, reporter output, targeted proteomics, and enzyme activity other than caspase-1. Use other_qualifying_endpoint only when the paper states an endpoint class that none of the above fits, and name that class in extra_details. Record the named platform, instrument, or panel only in analytical_platform_and_normalization, never here. Classifier or assay-performance results (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) are not a family: classify them by the underlying measurement and record the performance metric in endpoint_and_comparator, result_value, and result_unit. For a result that genuinely spans domains inseparably, choose the family of the dominant reported platform and note the other domains in extra_details. Null only when the paper gives no basis to assign a class; never use an unspecified or not-reported placeholder.

schema_spec.name: analytical_platform_and_normalization
schema_spec.description: Named analytical platform, assay technology, instrument or panel and the reported normalization, scaling, reference-gene, loading-control, internal-standard, batch-correction, or denominator method. Distinguish complementary platforms when they yield different metrics. Null when neither platform nor normalization is stated; never invent standard procedures or write not reported.

schema_spec.name: endpoint_and_comparator
schema_spec.description: Measured analyte, cytokine, enzyme activity, viability or synergy endpoint, gene or panel, pathway or signature, metabolite or lipid, miRNA, EV feature, phenotype, or classifier output, together with the measured quantity and the comparator or reference condition needed to interpret it, and any explicitly tested interaction claim such as sensitization, synergy, suppression, or protection. Name the quantity in words; the numeric unit or metric label belongs in result_unit and the measurement technology belongs in analytical_platform_and_normalization. Use one coherent endpoint per record and split distinct analyte-specific values, directions, or metrics. Null only if the endpoint cannot be named explicitly.

schema_spec.name: effect_direction
schema_spec.description: Overall reported status of the focal endpoint relative to its comparator. Choose exactly one: increased or decreased for a unidirectional change, whether or not it is an amplification of or protection against a co-administered challenge; no_change for an explicitly tested null effect; mixed when one retained record reports opposing directions across panel members, doses, or times, including an explicitly non-monotonic or biphasic response, with the specific pattern preserved in extra_details; below_detection only when undetectability itself is the reported outcome rather than a measured decrease. These values are mutually exclusive. Sensitization, synergy, suppression, and protection are interaction claims, not directions: state them in endpoint_and_comparator alongside the comparator. Missing or unestablished direction is null, never unspecified or unclear.

schema_spec.name: result_value
schema_spec.description: Single numeric treatment-effect, abundance, concentration, activity, fold change, percent change, pathway score, synergy metric, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, or other focal result for this record. Use the reported central or boundary value without conversion. Leave null for qualitative findings, unresolved ranges, or unavailable values; preserve qualifiers, uncertainty, and group values in extra_details.

schema_spec.name: result_unit
schema_spec.description: Unit or explicit metric label corresponding to result_value, such as pg/mL, percent, fold, ratio, activity units, pathway score, AUC, sensitivity, or specificity. Preserve the paper's unit without conversion. This field is meaningful only as the pair of result_value: leave it null whenever result_value is null, and also when result_value is reported but the paper supplies no unit or metric label. Never write dimensionless, unitless, not applicable, or not reported.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Additional explicit details needed to interpret the record but not represented above, including focal paper code/formulation, secondary identifiers, dose or time ranges, comparator group values, inequalities and uncertainty, statistical details, disease/genetic or nondefault conditions, donor/strain nuances, vehicle and formulation, culture conditions, sample preparation, EV isolation, instrument settings, ancillary findings, and mechanistic observations. Do not duplicate structured fields and never use this field merely to say that information was not reported.
